The test image shows a corn leaf with:
- Small circular tan/brown spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Some spots appear to have halos
- Small black dots visible near the midrib area
- Spots are randomly distributed

This pattern suggests Tar Spot (black stromata with fisheye halos) or Eyespot. Let me check the Tar Spot reference.

Comparing test vs. reference:
- The reference Tar Spot shows dense black stromata scattered across the leaf, with at least one fisheye lesion visible
- The test image has sparser distribution but shows small circular tan spots, some black dots near the midrib, and what could be early fisheye lesions (black dot with tan halo)

The test image appears to be an early/mild Tar Spot infection — the black dots near the midrib are stromata, and the tan circular spots are consistent with fisheye lesions forming. The pattern matches Tar Spot better than Eyespot (which would have more pronounced brown-purple rings) or Holcus Spot (which has larger lesions with distinct red-brown margins).
